architectureDecisions: D1: Use run --tool <id> --task <task.json> --recovery-dir <dir> for a first durable run and run --tool <id> --task <task.json> --resume-dir <dir> for explicit resume. Both are value-taking options compatible with parseOptions. They are mutually exclusive; repeating the first command against a handle remains HANDLE_CURRENT. No auto-resume based on file existence.

D2: In commandRun validate mode/path and all existing run factors first. Nonempty paths must contain non-whitespace characters; resolve them to absolute paths. Missing values already throw UsageError via parseOptions. Check both-mode conflict before task/handle I/O. Keep existing tool/task requirements and the general parser behavior for unrelated flags.

D3: Resume reads through readAgentToolRunHandle, verifies with verifyAgentToolRunHandle, and performs an operator preflight before executable resolution or observation construction: resolved handle.recoveryDir equals selected directory; validated task id/resolved repositoryRoot/baseRevision match the handle; requested tool id matches handle.toolId; status is RUNNING. Use exported RecoveryError with HANDLE_INVALID, TOOL_MISMATCH and HANDLE_COMPLETE. Never treat a read/verification error as permission to start.

D4: First-run calls runSupervisedTask with recoveryDir (null when omitted). Resume calls resumeSupervisedTask(handle, options) with the original task and resolved tool. Reuse the API checks for on-disk digest/currentness, source drift, missing worktree, session recovery and completed status; never construct a worktree/session, copy a handle or call harness.start in the CLI.

D5: Build one shared options tuple within commandRun for task/tool/model/timeoutMs/permissionProfile and the delivered observation hooks. Default first-run maxAttempts stays 3; omitted resume maxAttempts is null so the API uses handle.maxAttempts; supplied positive values are passed as the existing API permits. Preserve model null, timeout 600000, permission WORKSPACE_EDIT, arm validation, result finalization, printed JSON and 0/1/2 ACCEPTED/EXHAUSTED/TOOL_UNAVAILABLE exits.

D6: Durable start/resume retains the recovery directory on success and error exactly as the delivered API does. Do not call disposeRecoverableRun automatically in commandRun; document the existing API for explicit caller disposal and use it for test cleanup. A terminal handle is inspectable and an explicit later resume fails HANDLE_COMPLETE. Default nonrecoverable run keeps its current finally cleanup.

D7: UsageError retains exit 64 and usage text. RecoveryError follows the existing uncaught-error path: nonzero exit with its code in stderr, no result claiming ACCEPTED, no deletion/retry/fallback. Keep missing-tool TOOL_UNAVAILABLE exit 2 behavior after preflight. This task does not prescribe a new JSON error envelope or change other subcommands.

D8: The test file defines runCli as a subprocess harness around process.execPath and the absolute bin path with shell:false; it is not a mock or new exported product function. Each bound negative test calls runCli directly and asserts subject behavior. Use --command with an absolute generated .mjs wrapper around the existing fake-agent.mjs to record version probes as well as agent invocations; resolveExecutable already supports such scripts.

D9: Test actual CLI process death with a first verifier gate: it writes a readiness marker only after ACT_COMPLETED handle persistence, then waits on a test-owned release file with a bounded deadline. The parent test waits for the marker plus a verified RUNNING handle, kills the CLI process, releases/reaps the detached gate verifier, then invokes --resume-dir in a fresh CLI process. A second verifier is the failing sum test and fake PARTIAL_THEN_FIX exercises the same tool session on attempt 2. Do not expose a product crash flag or edit the delivered crash-supervised fixture.

D10: The CLI checks only delivered identity/path/tool/status and delegates resume semantics. Current BB-101 does not cryptographically bind prompt, verifications, model, permission or timeout; docs must state that callers resupply the original task/config. BB-125 owns stronger binding. If its delivered API changes before Worker start, recheck compatibility and return contradictions to research rather than implementing its contract here.

D11: Independent readiness and Worker evidence bind exact objective/plan/candidate hashes. Current research evidence is source inspection plus delivered API regression only; new CLI tests and feature acceptance are future Worker outputs.

negativeVerificationCases: Without recovery flags, ACCEPTED, EXHAUSTED and exception paths must leave no temporary worktree.
--recovery-dir on a directory with a RUNNING handle must return HANDLE_CURRENT, not automatically resume.
--resume-dir with a changed task id, resolved repositoryRoot or baseRevision must return HANDLE_INVALID.
--resume-dir with ACCEPTED, EXHAUSTED or TOOL_UNAVAILABLE must return HANDLE_COMPLETE and retain the terminal handle.
--resume-dir with no handle, malformed JSON or invalid handle shape must return HANDLE_INVALID; never reinterpret it as a first run.
--resume-dir with a changed body and old digest must return DIGEST_MISMATCH.
A valid RUNNING handle whose worktree was removed must return MISSING_WORKTREE, without creating a replacement.
A source commit after crash must produce SOURCE_HEAD_DRIFT; compare snapshots to the deliberately drifted state, not the original baseline.
A tool id different from handle.toolId must return TOOL_MISMATCH before any version probe or agent invocation.
A valid digest with handle.recoveryDir different from the selected --resume-dir must return HANDLE_INVALID without following the other directory.
Supplying --recovery-dir and --resume-dir together must return usage exit 64 before reading or changing either run.
Missing or empty recovery path values must return usage exit 64; quoted empty and whitespace-only values are invalid.
Non-positive/non-integer --max-attempts or --timeout-ms, and invalid --permission, must return usage exit 64 before first-run or resume.
--arm without --trace-dir must return usage exit 64 on start and resume without launching a process.
